Initial.Verbatim:
# Pre-run static review of DSP-004 OD04-A T0 dry run v2

I made no edits, ran nothing on Windows and used no network. Every line number below refers to the candidate files in `/mnt/user-data/outputs/dsp004-probe/v2/`.

**What I checked first.** All embedded SHA values match the actual bytes:
- `install_v2.ps1` L21–24 match `supervisor_v2.ps1`, `probe_v2.py`, `bound_list_v2.json` and `run_v2.cmd`.
- `supervisor_v2.ps1` L18 matches `bound_list_v2.json`.
- The SupervisorFiles byte counts are correct (2246 and 335).
- The 653 RuntimeFiles have exactly the same paths, byte counts and SHAs as the v1 `bound_list.json`.
- All six files are pure ASCII with no byte-order mark.
- The expected ACL strings (Base, Dir, File) are exactly the forms observed in the v1 raw records. The group SID in v1 was `S-1-5-21-…-513`, which contains no "D", so the group-stripping regex works.

## 1. Status of IR-01 to IR-14

| ID | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| IR-01 | **Partly resolved** | **Fixed:** absolute `powershell.exe` path; host and `$PSHOME` checks (L76–77); module autoload off and core modules only from `$PSHOME` (L11–15); supervisor, probe and bound list in an admin-only folder; bound-list SHA embedded; supervisor bytes anchored by the pre-run commit plus external read-back; AutoRun and file-association checks (L93–98). **Still open:** (a) nothing checks CLR environment injection into `powershell.exe` (`COR_ENABLE_PROFILING`/`COR_PROFILER_PATH`, `COMPlus_*`, `DOTNET_*`, `APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_*`). These come from user-writable HKCU\Environment and run user code inside the supervisor before L1. (b) The parent check (L81) accepts any `cmd.exe`; no command line is recorded, so nothing shows that `run_v2.cmd` launched the supervisor. (c) The PASS record is written by the supervisor into user-writable Documents (L28–29), and no external anchor covers it. (d) Anchor (a) is currently broken by git line-ending normalization (see W1). |
| IR-02 | **Mostly resolved** | Now checked from outside the child: loaded native modules, with a ≥10 non-empty guard (L218, L233–234); image path; parent PID; creation time; exit code; stderr content; tree scans before and after. Still the child's own report: the source-import closure, `MainFile`, flags and `sys.path`. The loader allowlist also has a `'type'` wildcard (R3). |
| IR-03 | **Not resolved** | This cannot be fixed at the same privilege level, and v2 adds nothing for it. It must be written in as a residual. It is wider than IR-03 said, because for an admin account UAC is not a security boundary (auto-elevation bypasses work at the default UAC level). |
| IR-04 | **Resolved** (record and enforce) | `IsInRole`, the whoami integrity SIDs and `EnableLUA` are recorded and enforced (L84–91). `ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin` and `PromptOnSecureDesktop` are not recorded. |
| IR-05 | **Mostly resolved** | The child environment is cleared to 4 fixed variables, recorded, and confirmed by the child (L203–207, L249). The `-X` flag is gone. No stdin data is sent. The OpenSSL config path is checked. Still open: the child still reads stdin (an empty pipe used to hold it, probe L119), which conflicts with PF-004's literal "no stdin". `sys.path` is recorded but never asserted. The OpenSSL config folder at L187 is assumed to be compiled into `libcrypto-3.dll`, not shown. The v2 approach also departs from design REV1 (`-X pycache_prefix`), and that departure needs to be recorded. |
| IR-06 | **Mostly resolved** | The tree must match the exact file set; `.pyc`, `.zip`, `._pth`, `pyvenv.cfg` and `__pycache__` are forbidden; the scan runs before and after; and every file and folder gets an ACL check (L133–168, L256–258). Loader coverage is still the child's own report. |
| IR-07 | **Not resolved** (recorded only) | The KnownDLLs list is recorded (L193–194). The bytes actually mapped into memory are still not bound. Accept it as a residual. |
| IR-08 | **Largely resolved** | Authenticode is checked on 44 PE files (L170–184), and the external CPython-tag comparison covers Lib. Still open: the signer check is an unanchored substring `O=…` match with no thumbprint or root pin, and a "Valid" result also trusts the CurrentUser root store. Also, the "603 Lib/*.py" figure is really 603 Lib files: 595 `.py` plus 8 other files (including the pip `.whl`, which is binary, so "modulo LF→CRLF" does not apply to it). |
| IR-09 | **Partly resolved** | The installer records its own SHA (a self re-read, as weak as v1's) and a timestamp. The pre-run commit and the read-back cover the four installed files. Still open: the installer still runs elevated from user-writable Documents. The elevated `cmd.exe` running `install_v2.cmd` executes the user-writable HKCU AutoRun and inherits HKCU environment variables (including the CLR profiler variables). That is a user-to-admin path that `install_v2.ps1` never checks. |
| IR-10 | **Resolved procedurally, if followed** | This needs commit and merge time < `InstalledUtc` < `StartedUtc`, shown from records. This review shares a model family with the author. |
| IR-11 | **Partly resolved** | The v2 record contains no user-specific paths, so it can be committed raw, and `ReportLine` keeps the child's raw line. Its SHA is fixed only when the recorder reads it back, and it can be forged before that. It also needs `-text` in git (W1). |
| IR-12 | **Resolved** | The probe sits under admin-only parent folders, so a user cannot place a junction above it. |
| IR-13 | **Mostly resolved** | Creation time is now captured, stderr content is checked, and `__pycache__` is scanned after the run. The −50 ms tolerance at L232 points the wrong way for a proof (R4). |
| IR-14 | **Not resolved** | Read and execute are still granted to the whole BUILTIN\Users group, not a run account. Folders below the base still inherit, whereas the design says "inheritance off". The group-stripping regex is unchanged; it still fails closed. |

## 2. Bugs on Windows PowerShell 5.1

**What I checked and found sound:**
- The `Import-Module` paths for the Utility and Security `.psd1` files exist in 5.1.
- Every module-qualified cmdlet belongs to the module named: `Add-Type`, `ConvertTo-Json` and `ConvertFrom-Json` are Utility; `Get-Acl` and `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` are Security.
- Unqualified `New-Object` and `Sort-Object` are Utility cmdlets, but they are only called after Utility has been imported.
- No StrictMode trap: all 653 entries carry a `SignerOrg` key, and `[ordered]` dot-assignment works.
- `ConvertFrom-Json` handles the 122 KB bound list and a null line (the null case is caught at L223).
- `ManagementObjectSearcher` with indexers and `ManagementDateTimeConverter` behave as intended.
- whoami CSV on zh-CN: SIDs are ASCII and quoted, so the regex at L86–87 works.
- Registry reads: `EnableLUA` comes back as Int32 1.
- `ReadLineAsync` and `ReadToEndAsync` cannot deadlock (both reads start before the child's roughly 20 KB write).
- `$entries`/`$held` indexes stay aligned (`$held[0]` is the bound list, and any failure to lock calls `Block`).
- Locks use share-read, which allows Python's own opens and LoadLibrary (FILE_SHARE_READ covers execute access). v1 already showed this works.
- ACL and owner on files created by `install_v2`: elevated `CreateNew` → `icacls /reset` → `/setowner BA` produces the expected Dir and File forms.
- Authenticode: catalog-signed System32 DLLs return "Valid" in PS 5.1 with subject "CN=Microsoft Windows, O=Microsoft Corporation…", which matches. `vcruntime140*.dll` is Microsoft-signed and matches. PS opens catalog files with share-read, which does not conflict with the held handles.
- Child environment: `EnvironmentVariables.Clear()` plus 4 variables is fine; Python skips the `=C:` variables.
- Frozen and built-in stdlib modules report loader name `'type'` and origin `'frozen'`/`'built-in'`, so they correctly drop out of the source-module check.

### WILL_FAIL (blocks or false-fails the run)

| ID | Where | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | Repo commit | The root `.gitattributes` is `* text=auto eol=lf`, and a v2 folder would inherit it (I confirmed with `git check-attr`: `text: auto`). `supervisor_v2.ps1`, `install_v2.ps1`, `probe_v2.py` and both `.cmd` files are CRLF. Committed as-is, they become LF blobs, so the committed bytes ≠ the embedded SHAs and anchor (a) is false. If the owner takes the files from a checkout, the installer stops with `SOURCE_SHA_MISMATCH_*`. The v1 folder avoided this with its own `.gitattributes` containing `* -text`. |
| W2 | `bound_list_v2.json` SystemDlls | These 22 hashes are from the 2026-10-31 machine state. Any cumulative or preview update before the run (the November Patch Tuesday is 2026-11-10) blocks with `HASH_MISMATCH`. The OS build/UBR is not recorded either. |
| W3 | supervisor L28–29, L38 | If `Documents\dsp004-probe` does not exist, `Write-Record` throws, so neither a PASS nor a `Block` writes any record. |
| W4 | supervisor L98 | An existing HKCU or HKLM AutoRun (conda init and clink set one) or any HKCU `Classes\.cmd` key blocks the run. This fails closed, but it is likely on developer machines. |
| W5 | supervisor L174–178 | The PSF/Microsoft signer org for all 44 runtime PE files is assumed, not shown in any record. If any one is unsigned or signed differently, the run blocks. |
| W6 | supervisor L218, L54, L162 and others | There is no `trap`. A transient exception (for example `Process.Modules` throwing a Win32Exception, or WMI or `Get-Acl` failing) ends the script with no record. |

### WRONG_RESULT (could pass when it should fail)

| ID | Where | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | supervisor L71–98 and install L37–42 | CLR profiler / AppDomainManager environment variables are not checked, and the host's own loaded modules (`$me.Modules`) are not enumerated. User code inside `powershell.exe` can falsify every check while every hijack check passes. |
| R2 | supervisor L177–178, L181 | The signer test is an unanchored `-notmatch 'O=…'`, with no thumbprint or chain-root pin and no `IsOSBinary` check for system DLLs. "Valid" also honours roots in the CurrentUser store. |
| R3 | probe L109 and supervisor L248 | Built-in and frozen loaders are classes, so the probe reports them as `'type'`. The `'BuiltinImporter'` and `'FrozenImporter'` entries never match, and `'type'` admits any loader that is a class. A module with no spec (`Loader=None`) is also allowed. |
| R4 | supervisor L232 | `AddMilliseconds(-50)` accepts a child created up to 50 ms before T0. Some tolerance is needed, because the kernel's CreateTime is tick-coarse while .NET 4.6+ `UtcNow` is precise. But the check proves only "not earlier than T0 − 50 ms", and it must be labelled that way. |
| R5 | supervisor L54/L59, L81, L243 | No command line is captured for the supervisor, its parent or the child. The design's caller identity includes "command line". `MainFile` and argv rest only on the child's report, even though WMI `CommandLine` would give an outside check. |

### MINOR

- `install_v2.ps1` L71: `InstallerSha256` is a self re-read and proves nothing. L59/L61: the meaning of `icacls /C` exit codes is unverified.
- `supervisor_v2.ps1` L102: the bound list is read with a single `Read()` call that is not looped. In practice this is fine for a local file.
- `sys.path` is not asserted. Under `-I`, the 3.12 path calculation skips the registry, so the risk is low.
- L189: `OpenSslModulesDirPresent` is recorded but never blocks.
- Neither the host's SHA nor the OS build/UBR is recorded.

## 3. Gaps that would still make a PASS non-evidentiary

1. **Trust root.** Everything still runs at the owner's medium integrity level. The record is self-written into a user-writable folder and can be deleted and rerun or forged; nothing counts runs. V3.2 §6.1 and `bootstrap_evidence_reference` require "detached trusted startup/environment evidence". No such evidence exists. Process-creation auditing (event 4688 with command line, plus 4689) written by the system and exported after the run would supply it.
2. **ACL layer against a same-user adversary.** The owner is an admin, and UAC is not a boundary for admin accounts. The design's "run account" (a separate standard user) is not used.
3. **Gaps that stay open by design:** IR-03 (process tampering), IR-07 (KnownDLLs, and modules loaded and unloaded between snapshots), the source-import closure being the child's own report, and n=1.
4. **Upstream mismatches.** V3.2 §3 says "Recorded Python 3.12.13", but the runtime is 3.12.10. §6.1 says "no new verifier, launcher … authorized here", so v2 needs its own owner authorization.
5. **Read-back anchors (b) and (c)** pass through a bridge in the owner's session. They are independent of the supervisor, but not of that session.

## 4. Verdict: (b) fit to run only after the must-fix items

Even with every fix below, a PASS can count only as a non-evidentiary engineering observation that depends on the owner's session being uncompromised, unless gap 1 is also closed.

**Must-fix:**
1. **Repo:** before committing, add `.gitattributes` with `* -text` in the v2 asset folder (the same file as in the v1 folder). Then check that `git ls-files --eol` shows `i/crlf` for the 5 CRLF files and that the blob bytes' SHAs equal the constants.
2. **supervisor_v2.ps1, after L98:** block if any environment variable name matches `^(COR_ENABLE_PROFILING|COR_PROFILER(_PATH(_32|_64)?)?|COMPLUS_.*|DOTNET_.*|APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_.*)$` (record the names only). Also enumerate `$me.Modules` and block if any `FileName` is outside `$WinDir\`.
3. **install_v2.ps1, after L38:** add the same environment-variable and module check, plus the AutoRun and `.cmd`/`cmdfile` checks copied from supervisor L94–98. Record the results in `install_v2_result.json`.
4. **supervisor_v2.ps1 L54/L59:** add `CommandLine` to the WMI query and to the returned record.
   - At L81, also require the parent's command line to contain the full path of `$SupDir\run_v2.cmd`.
   - After L231, add `OI_ChildCommandLineExact`: `$ci.CommandLine -ceq ('"' + $PyExe + '" ' + $argv)`.
5. **supervisor_v2.ps1 L67:** call `[IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($OutDir)` first. Add a top-level `trap` that writes a `BLOCKED UNEXPECTED_EXCEPTION` record.
6. **Before the run, write into the pre-run record:** the residuals (IR-03, admin-account UAC, the record being self-written, IR-07, n=1); the −50 ms meaning of L232; and a statement that system-DLL hashes are pinned to the current OS build. Run before any Windows update.
7. **Then regenerate in order:** the probe and `.cmd` SHAs, then `bound_list_v2.json`, then L18, then install L21–24. Re-review the changed bytes before committing.

**Should-fix:**
- At L177–181, pin the signer certificate thumbprint or chain root, and require `IsOSBinary` for system DLLs.
- At probe L109, report `loader.__name__` when the loader is a class, and drop `'type'` at L248.
- Assert `sys.path` against the expected 4 entries.
- Record the OS build/UBR and the SHA of `powershell.exe`.
- Confirm the OpenSSL config folder by reading the string out of the read-back copy of `libcrypto-3.dll`.
- Enable process-creation auditing (4688 with command line) during install, and export it after the run as detached evidence.

## Re-review of the changed v2 bytes

I made no edits, changed no git state and used no network.

**Verdict: fit to run now with no further code changes.** It still needs the commit-time step (folder `.gitattributes` with `* -text`, then a blob-SHA check), the pre-run residuals record, and the owner's authorization for the v2 launcher. A PASS remains a non-evidentiary engineering observation, as stated before; the gaps in section 3 of my earlier report are unchanged.

### (3) SHA constants: all match the current bytes

| File | SHA-256 | Size | Bound where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supervisor_v2.ps1` | `2CCFCDD4…0A527F` | 21942 | install L21 |
| `probe_v2.py` | `EE0BFD1E…822AC0` | 2373 | install L22 and the bound list |
| `bound_list_v2.json` | `8FE6ECF6…C2801E` | 143291 | install L23 and supervisor L18 |
| `run_v2.cmd` | `57B23F6B…C1BDD` | 335 | install L24 and the bound list |
| `install_v2.ps1` | `BF5F8A84…54E2B9` | 6504 | (not self-bound) |

Other byte-level checks:
- The bound list's 653 runtime entries and 22 system-DLL entries are byte-identical in path, size and SHA to v1. All 653 carry both `SignerOrg` and `SignerThumbprint`, so there is no StrictMode trap. All 44 PE files have a thumbprint (39, 2 and 1 for the PSF files, plus 2 distinct Microsoft ones).
- All files are ASCII. Line endings are unchanged: CRLF everywhere except the bound list, which is LF. So the `-text` step is still required.

### (1) Are must-fix 2–5 and R2–R4 implemented correctly?

**Yes. I found no defects.**

- **Must-fix 2:** supervisor L93–103.
- **Must-fix 3:** install L42–54.
- **Must-fix 4:** supervisor L57/L62, L87, L88 and L260.
- **Must-fix 5:** supervisor L70, L72 and L43–46.
- **R2:** supervisor L199–208.
- **R3:** probe L124–125, supervisor L276–277. In v1's data, the only modules with no loader were `__main__`, `typing.io` and `typing.re`, and the last two have no origin, so they pass.
- **R4:** supervisor L259.
- **sys.path assertion (L278–279):** the expected list matches the 4 entries v1 actually observed, in the same order.

### (2) New WILL_FAIL or WRONG_RESULT from these edits

**No new WILL_FAIL that blocks a clean machine. No new serious WRONG_RESULT.** Point by point:

- **`trap` in PS 5.1:** a trap applies to its whole scope, whatever line it sits on. So it also catches errors before L72. An error before L44 (for example at the L14–16 imports) runs the trap before `Block` exists, so the script ends with no record (MINOR). After L44 the behaviour is correct:
  - Errors inside functions and pipeline script blocks reach the trap.
  - The local `try`/`catch` blocks (L123, L138, L250) still take precedence.
  - The re-entry guard turns a failing `Write-Record` into `exit 5` instead of an endless loop.
  - A child left waiting on stdin gets end-of-file when the supervisor exits, so it does not hang.
- **`IsOSBinary`:** this property exists on PS 5.1's `Signature` object on Windows 10/11 (alongside `SignatureType`), and is reported True for catalog-signed System32 files and for `powershell.exe`. Reading it through `PSObject.Properties` fails closed if it is missing. I cannot confirm it on the owner's build, but at worst this means a `SIGNATURE_PROBLEM` block, not a false pass.
- **`$me.Modules` on `powershell.exe`:** this works. The Defender AMSI provider (`MpOav.dll` under ProgramData) has subject `O=Microsoft Corporation` and is accepted. Two side effects:
  - **Conditional fail-closed:** a third-party antivirus that registers an AMSI provider or injects a DLL (common on zh-CN machines) will block with `HOST_MODULE_UNTRUSTED`, in both the installer and the supervisor.
  - **New WRONG_RESULT (MINOR):** L98 and install L52 accept any module under `C:\Windows\` without a signature check, including user-writable folders such as `C:\Windows\Temp`, `Tasks` and `tracing`. Narrowing this to `System32`, `WinSxS`, `Microsoft.NET` and `assembly`, or signature-checking every module, would close it. It matters only if a DLL has already been injected, which is the IR-03 residual anyway.
- **Parent command line:** an Explorer double-click gives `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /c ""C:\Program Files\DSP004Runtime\supervisor_v2\run_v2.cmd" "`, which contains the path, so L87 passes. Launching from an already-open cmd window or a shortcut with a short path blocks (fail-closed). Tell the owner to double-click `run_v2.cmd` in Explorer. The check is a substring match, so it can be spoofed with a crafted cmd line (MINOR, same-user residual).
- **`OI_ChildCommandLineExact`:** .NET Framework builds the command line as `"` + FileName + `"` + space + Arguments, without re-quoting an unquoted FileName. That gives exactly `"C:\Program Files\DSP004Runtime\Python312\python.exe" -I -S -B "C:\Program Files\DSP004Runtime\supervisor_v2\probe_v2.py"`. WMI returns the process's command line verbatim, so the case-sensitive `-ceq` is correct.
- **Thumbprint pins:** these are fail-closed only if the offline derivation took the **primary** signer. That is the outer PKCS#7 SignerInfo, not a nested or dual signature, and it is what Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports. If a nested signer was used, the run blocks with `SIGNATURE_PROBLEM`. It cannot cause a false pass.
- **StrictMode:** I found no new traps. L87, L91, L201 and L203 are all safe.
- **Carry-over (not new):** the system-DLL hashes are still pinned to the 2026-10-31 OS state. The build/UBR is now recorded, but any Windows update installed before the run blocks with `HASH_MISMATCH`.

### (4) Remaining items before the run

There are no code must-fix items left.

**Required at commit and before the run:**
1. Add `.gitattributes` with `* -text` to the v2 folder. After committing, confirm `git ls-files --eol` shows `i/crlf` for the five CRLF files and that the committed blob bytes hash to the constants above.
2. Write the pre-run residuals record, as must-fix 6 (IR-03 process tampering, the admin account under UAC, the self-written record, KnownDLLs, n=1, the −50 ms meaning of L259). Get the owner's explicit authorization for this new launcher, since V3.2 §6.1 says no new launcher is authorized there.
3. Run before any Windows update; double-click `run_v2.cmd` in Explorer; and make sure no third-party antivirus has DLLs loaded into PowerShell (or accept the fail-closed block).

**Optional:** narrow the `C:\Windows` exemption at L98 and install L52. The L213 comment still asserts, without proof, that the OpenSSL config path is compiled into `libcrypto-3.dll`.
